GLA.about: GLA (evening primrose oil): for atopic dermatitis in children there are indications of benefit in case of poor quality of work; Ineffective for acne and psoriasis.
GLA.caution: Ineffective for acne, psoriasis, chronic manual dermatitis, hepatitis B, preeclampsia and Sjögren's syndrome.
GLA.course: A course of weeks-months according to schemes from research; exact terms are not given in abstracts.
GLA.food_sources: Flax, hemp, and soy contain trace amounts of GLA; a practical source is evening primrose seed oil.
GLA.guidelines: EAACI 2024: Insufficient evidence for evening primrose. Review 2024: No strong recommendations for inflammatory conditions due to heterogeneity.
GLA.how_to_choose: For skin - Oenothera biennis oil; take into account the low quality of research. For arthritis and diabetes, there is insufficient data to make a choice.
mechs: Substrate for prostaglandins and anti-inflammatory mediators
Relief of symptoms of atopic dermatitis
Support barrier function and skin hydration
Improved skin condition in healthy volunteers
Metabolism of GLA into leukotrienes and anti-inflammatory mediators
GLA.myths: “Primrose heals the skin” - data relate to atopic dermatitis in children. “It will help with joints” - with rheumatoid arthritis, the results are mixed. “Proven” - quality according to Jadad is low, review 2024 requires caution.
GLA.name: GLA
GLA.onset: Within the framework of the reception, weeks-months; for dermatitis, the assessment is based on the SCORAD scale, the rate in abstracts is not specified.
GLA.title: GLA
GLA.who_needs: Children with atopic dermatitis without food allergies - there is evidence of improvement in symptoms. Ineffective for acne, psoriasis, PMS, dry eyes and preeclampsia.
